Medical & Emergency Contacts.situation: Fire, Traffic Accident, or Medical Emergency (119)
advices: Dial 119 for the Fire station or Ambulance.
When to use: When encountering a fire or a severe traffic accident. Use this number when there is a seriously injured or seriously sick person.
When to use: When encountering a traffic accident or when encountering criminal actions such as theft or violence.
Dial 050-3816-2787 for the Japan Visitor Hotline (JNTO Call Center).
When to use: Call for general tourist information or for multilingual assistance in case of accidents or emergencies.
Dial 118 for the Japan Coast Guard.
When to use: For emergencies at sea, such as boating accidents, drownings, or if someone falls into the ocean.

Medical & Emergency Contacts.situation: Medical Consultation / Unsure if it's an emergency
advices: Dial #7119 for the Emergency Medical Consultation Center.

When to use: If you are feeling suddenly unwell or injured but aren't sure if it's severe enough to call an ambulance (119) or if you should just visit a hospital yourself. Medical specialists will advise you on what to do.
Dial 03-6233-9266 for the AMDA International Medical Information Center.
When to use: They provide multilingual support to help foreigners find clinics and hospitals that speak their language, and they can explain how the Japanese medical system works.

Medical & Emergency Contacts.situation: Mental Health Support or Travel Stress
advices: When to use: A dedicated, confidential English-speaking lifeline for mental health crises, severe travel stress, or counseling.

Medical & Emergency Contacts.situation: Hokkaido Local Support and Disaster Navigation
advices: Dial 011-200-9595 for the Hokkaido Foreign Resident Support Center.

When to use: This is a highly relevant local number for Hokkaido. They offer multilingual consultation services regarding local medical care inquiries, disaster support, and navigating Hokkaido's systems.
